payload.note: The cricothyroid membrane's inferior border is the superior border of the cricoid cartilage. Operational DEPENDS_ON test (Law 8): remove the cricoid cartilage now and the membrane loses its inferior anchor — it can no longer function as the fibrous sheet between the two cartilages that serves as the emergency airway landmark. The membrane's defined role requires both attachment points to exist. Not identity (the membrane is fibrous tissue, the cricoid is cartilage) and not purpose (Law 8c).

payload.name: stylohyoid-ligament
payload.scope: People made the stylohyoid ligament construct to map the band suspending the hyoid bone from the styloid process of the skull, so that anatomists and skull-base surgeons can orient the hyoid suspensions and diagnose its calcifications causing Eagle syndrome.

definition.body: The stylohyoid ligament is a human-authored anatomical construct mapping the band of fibrous tissue connecting the styloid process of the temporal bone to the greater horn of the hyoid bone, suspending the hyoid from the skull base. Parameters: (1) the attachments - the styloid process of the temporal bone superiorly, the greater horn of the hyoid bone inferiorly; (2) the structure - a flat fibrous band approximately 3 cm long through which the stylohyoid muscle passes, the ligament remaining behind it; (3) the function - transmitting force between the skull base and the hyoid and limiting hyoid excursion during swallowing and mastication; (4) the clinical significance - calcification and elongation of the ligament and styloid process producing the pain of Eagle syndrome. It persists as a standard anatomical structure in human anatomy texts, skull-base surgical references, and radiology. e.g.: the stylohyoid ligament depicted in the skull chapter of Moore Clinically Orientated Anatomy, 9th edition; stylohyoid ligament calcification on lateral skull radiograph in Eagle syndrome in a radiology teaching file; the stylohyoid ligament preserved in a parotidectomy approach in a head and neck surgery atlas | not: the stylohyoid muscle (the muscle passing through the ligament, a distinct structure); the styloid process (the bone to which the ligament attaches); the temporomandibular joint (the mandibular articulation, a different relation) [formal: ligamentum stylohyoideum | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]

payload.name: paraglottic-space
payload.scope: People made the paraglottic space construct to map the fat-filled lateral compartment of the larynx, so that radiologists and head and neck surgeons can assess tumor spread in laryngeal cancer staging and plan surgical approaches.

definition.body: The paraglottic space is a human-authored anatomical construct mapping the potential fat-filled compartment on each side of the larynx, bounded medially by the perichondrium of the thyroid lamina and laterally by the thyrohyoid membrane, extending from the hyoid to the cricoid, that provides the plane of tumor spread in laryngeal carcinoma. Parameters: (1) the boundaries - medially the perichondrium of the thyroid lamina, laterally the thyrohyoid membrane inferiorly blending into the cricothyroid membrane, superiorly at the level of the hyoid, inferiorly at the cricoid; (2) the contents - fat and loose connective tissue with lymphatic channels, carrying the recurrent laryngeal nerve and the inferior laryngeal vessels in its lateral part; (3) the relations - the lateral continuation of the pre-epiglottic space, the two together enclosing the larynx; (4) the clinical significance - the plane of spread of T2 laryngeal carcinoma, with invasion of the space, loss of the fat plane on CT or MRI, marking T3 staging. It persists as a maintained anatomical landmark in head and neck radiology, laryngeal cancer staging, and surgical planning. e.g.: the paraglottic space evaluated on axial CT in AJCC staging of laryngeal carcinoma; paraglottic fat plane loss on MRI marking extralaryngeal extension of a T3 glottic cancer; the paraglottic space opened during a hemilaryngofissure approach in a head and neck surgery atlas | not: the pre-epiglottic space (the anterior compartment bounded by the thyroepiglottic ligament, a distinct compartment); the paralaryngeal space (the lateral neck space outside the larynx, including the strap muscles); the paraglottic perichondrium (the medial boundary, not the space) [formal: spatium paraglotticum | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]

payload.name: laryngocele
payload.scope: People made the laryngocele construct to map the cystic distension of the laryngeal saccule, so that otolaryngologists and head and neck surgeons can diagnose and excise the internal and external neck masses it produces.

definition.body: The laryngocele is a human-authored anatomical construct mapping the mucosa-lined cystic distension of the laryngeal saccule, filled with air or mucus, of the internal kind remaining within the larynx and the external kind extending through the thyrohyoid membrane into the neck. Parameters: (1) the origin - distension of the laryngeal saccule, the blind pouch of the anterior laryngeal ventricle; (2) the types - internal, confined within the larynx and distending the ventricular area, external, protruding through the thyrohyoid membrane, and combined; (3) the contents - air in a congenital laryngocele that still communicates with the ventricle, mucus in an acquired laryngocele whose neck is occluded; (4) the clinical significance - a neck mass fluctuating with straining or Valsalva, airway obstruction or hoarseness, treated by excision of the saccule. It persists as a standard diagnostic and surgical entity in otolaryngology, head and neck surgery, and radiology. e.g.: an external laryngocele as a neck mass fluctuating with Valsalva on CT in Cummings Otolaryngology, 6th edition; an internal laryngocele visualized on flexible laryngoscopy in Bailey's Head and Neck Otolaryngology; transoral excision of a laryngocele with saccule removal in a Laryngoscope case report | not: a thyroglossal duct cyst (midline embryological remnant, different origin); the laryngeal saccule (the normal blind pouch that the laryngocele distends); a pre-epiglottic abscess (an infection, not a saccule distension) [formal: laryngocele | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]

payload.note: The laryngocele's definition carves its origin as distension of the laryngeal saccule (parameter 1), and the laryngeal ventricle's accepted definition carves the saccule as the blind pouch of the ventricle's anterior portion (parameters 2 and 3). Operational test (Law 8): remove the laryngeal ventricle now and the saccule with it - the mapped cystic distension has nothing to distend and the construct ceases to operate. Not identity (a distension of a pouch is not the pouch or the ventricle) and not purpose (Law 8c): the laryngocele is a clinical entity that needs the ventricle's saccule to exist.
